reviewed: Agent review of arXiv:2506.22373v2 with paper2agent, 17 Oct 2026: agents re-ran the authors' notebooks and tested the claims with the verified code
verdict: The authors' code reproduces the Table II means, but the central claim doesn't hold: fitted the same way, a plain ΛCDM universe gives the same j₀ ≈ 2.3 and an equal or larger tension. The analysis measures the series' truncation error; it doesn't test ΛCDM.

claims.claim: Fitted to BAO and supernovae, the jerk j₀ sits above ΛCDM's j₀ = 1 (Table II).
claims.check: The four emcee notebooks re-run at the authors' settings reproduce the Table II means; the 2σ limits agree only roughly.

claims.claim: The departure from ΛCDM reaches 5.4σ with DESY5 supernovae.
claims.check: The σ is (mean(j₀) − 1)/std of a skewed marginal. A profile likelihood gives 3.9σ; widening the s₀ prior gives 3.7σ.

claims.claim: The data favour j₀ ≠ 1, a sign of physics beyond ΛCDM.
claims.check: Noiseless ΛCDM mocks fitted the same way give j₀ ≈ 2.3 and a spurious 2.8–5.4σ tension: the fit measures the series' truncation error.

claims.claim: The 12 DESI DR2 distances are used as published (Table I).
claims.check: Values and covariance compared with the official DESI DR2 file; the Lyα pair is combined correctly (D_V/rₛ = 31.27 ± 0.26).

main_problems: At the ΛCDM truth the 4th-order series misses the Lyα D_V point by 7.9% (9.7σ), so a high j₀ is what the shortcut gives, not new physics.
s₀ ends on its prior bound (10.0) in every fit and corr(j₀, s₀) ≈ 0.99; wider priors move DESY5 from 5.4σ to 3.7σ.
The quoted σ comes from a skewed marginal; a profile likelihood gives 2.1, 2.9, 3.3 and 3.9σ.
The DESY5 covariance is missing from the code release; the public copy gives χ²/dof 0.90, not 1.01.
No seed or convergence checks, and the H₀ prior is 50–90 in the code but 50–70 in the paper.

pins.title: DESI distances
pins.basic: 12 distance measurements copied straight from DESI's own published release.
pins.researcher: Values and covariance are byte-identical to the official DESI DR2 likelihood file. The Lyα D_M, D_H pair is correctly combined into D_V/rₛ = 31.27 ± 0.26 using their correlation (r = −0.43).

pins.title: Model curves only
pins.basic: No measurements: the curves show how far the shortcut strays from a plain ΛCDM universe. Its plotting code isn't in the repository.
pins.researcher: 2nd-, 3rd- and 4th-order y-series vs flat ΛCDM (H₀ = 70, Ωm = 0.3, so q₀ = −0.55, j₀ = 1, s₀ = −0.35), up to each probe's top data redshift (dashed). No plotting code in the repository; the review rebuilt the curves.

pins.title: Too blurry
pins.basic: The four-number shortcut is too blurry for data this sharp: it finds a jerk near 2 even in a plain ΛCDM universe.
pins.researcher: At the ΛCDM truth the series misses the Lyα D_V point by 7.9% (9.7σ). Noiseless ΛCDM mocks give a best-fit j₀ ≈ 2.3 and a spurious 2.8–5.4σ tension.

pins.title: The model
pins.basic: Describes the expansion with four numbers (speed, slow-down, jerk, snap) instead of a physical theory.
pins.researcher: 4th-order Taylor series of a(t) in y = z/(1+z), with distances from Eqs. 9–12. The code is correct, but printed Eq. 9 has a sign typo: +(5/3)q₀j₀, not −.

pins.title: Authors' MCMC chains
pins.basic: Likely values from the authors' fits to DESI, alone and with three supernova sets. Re-running their code gives the same averages.
pins.researcher: Posteriors from the four emcee notebooks (DESI DR2 BAO alone, + Union3, + Pantheon+, + DESY5). Re-run at the authors' settings, they reproduce the Table II means (j₀ 1.77, 1.93, 1.96, 2.05 vs 2.04); the 2σ limits agree only roughly.

pins.title: Hits a wall
pins.basic: One of the four numbers presses against the edge of its allowed range, and that edge decides the answer.
pins.researcher: The best-fit s₀ is 10.0, the prior bound, in every fit, and corr(j₀, s₀) ≈ 0.99. Widening the priors moves DESY5 from 5.4σ to 3.7σ by the paper's own measure.

pins.title: The fit
pins.basic: Tries millions of combinations of the four numbers and keeps the ones that match the data.
pins.researcher: emcee, 100 walkers × 21,000 steps, flat priors (H₀ 50–90 in the code but 50–70 in the paper; s₀ −10 to 10). No seed and no convergence checks.

pins.title: Supernovae
pins.basic: Three supernova catalogues. Only the shape of their distance curve counts, not how bright they are.
pins.researcher: Pantheon+ (1701, no redshift cut), Union3 (22 bins), DESY5 (1829). The magnitude offset is marginalised, which the paper doesn't state. The DESY5 covariance is missing from the code release; the public copy gives χ²/dof 0.90, not 1.01.

pins.title: What 5.4σ means
pins.basic: How far j₀ = 1 (plain ΛCDM) sits from the average answer, counted in units of spread.
pins.researcher: The quoted σ is (mean(j₀) − 1)/std of a skewed marginal; re-runs give 1.96, 3.43, 4.01 and 5.42. A profile likelihood gives 2.1, 2.9, 3.3 and 3.9σ.

pins.title: Sound horizon
pins.basic: A cosmic ruler length is fixed by hand, and it sets the H₀ value directly.
pins.researcher: rₛ = 148.3 Mpc is fixed (the DESY5 notebook uses 143.9). BAO only constrain H₀·rₛ, and the ±4.3 Mpc error on rₛ is not propagated into H₀.

pins.title: Wrong way round
pins.basic: DESI's dark-energy result predicts a jerk below 1. This paper finds above 1, yet calls the two consistent.
pins.researcher: For CPL, j₀ = 1 + (3/2)(1 − Ωₘ)[3w₀(1 + w₀) + wₐ]. DESI DR2's w₀wₐ fits give j₀ ≈ −0.06 to −0.77.
